title: Referential Uncertainty in Human--AI Collaboration
abstract: arXiv:2609.39518v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Effective human-AI collaboration requires partners to establish references through interaction, which becomes fragile when descriptions are ambiguous, similar referents compete, or partners see different things. We study referential uncertainty - uncertainty over which candidate object a description refers to - in a collaborative puzzle task where a human Helper instructs an AI Worker to place pieces. The Worker must identify and communicate its uncertainty, and the Helper must recognize and act on it. We show that a separately elicited belief distribution over candidate pieces is better calibrated (ECE 0.15) and better discriminates correct from incorrect placements (AUROC 0.65) than raw action-token probabilities, which are severely overconfident (0.97 mean confidence, ECE 0.44). translated_title: 人机协作中的指称不确定性
translated_abstract: 有效的“人—AI”协作要求合作双方通过交互建立指称关系，但当描述含糊不清、相似的指称对象相互竞争、或双方所见内容不同时，这种指称关系就会变得脆弱。我们在一个协作拼图任务中研究“指称不确定性”（即某个描述究竟指向哪个候选对象的不确定性），在该任务中，人类“助手”指示AI“执行者”放置拼图碎片。执行者必须识别并传达自身的不确定性，而助手必须识别这种不确定性并据此采取行动。我们证明，单独引出的关于候选碎片的信念分布比原始动作词元概率具有更好的校准性（ECE 0.15），并能更好地区分正确与错误的放置（AUROC 0.65）；而原始动作词元概率则严重过度自信（平均置信度0.97，ECE 0.44）。在三个前沿视觉-语言模型上，这种引出的不确定性随指令模糊程度的增加而可预测地上升，但并不随……（原文摘要在此处截断）。
tldr: 该论文在人机协作拼图任务中提出通过单独引出AI对候选对象的信念分布来度量指称不确定性，其校准性和区分正确与错误放置的能力显著优于原始动作词元概率，且随指令模糊程度可预测地变化。
en_tdlr: In a human-AI collaborative puzzle task, separately elicited belief distributions over candidate objects measure referential uncertainty far better than raw action-token probabilities, showing superior calibration and discrimination while rising predictably with instruction vagueness.
